title: AIA fetch loop: no aggregate byte cap
description: build_with_aia (pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:595-721) fetches intermediates via AIA caIssuers URIs and adds them to a CertPool. Bounded by AIA_MAX_DEPTH=5 iterations but no aggregate byte cap. What goes wrong (availability): memory growth from attacker-controlled AIA chains. Location: pkix-chain/src/lib.rs lines 607-700. Fix: aggregate byte counter in the loop.
close_reason:
WRONG AS FILED -- the aggregate cap the bead says is missing exists, is enforced, and is tested with an adversarial fixture.

The bead: "Bounded by AIA_MAX_DEPTH=5 iterations but no aggregate byte cap ... memory growth from attacker-controlled AIA chains. Fix: aggregate byte counter in the loop."

AiaConfig::max_total_fetches (default 8) is that aggregate bound. ChainBuildState seeds fetches_left from it (sans_io.rs:89), decrements by the number of new URIs per round (:203), and on exhaustion fails with Error::AiaFetchLimitExceeded { limit } (:173). It is a cap across the WHOLE reassembly, not per round, so it is not weakened by the depth loop.

Four further bounds the bead does not account for:
- tried_uris: every URI is fetched at most once across the whole reassembly, so a repeated URI cannot drain the budget again
- max_certs_per_response (default 16) caps what parse_ca_issuers_response will extract, so retained certificates are bounded by 8 x 16 = 128
- the pool refuses a certificate it already holds, so duplicates add nothing
- a 30s deadline

Net effect with the shipped fetcher: transient bytes <= 8 fetches x DEFAULT_MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE (1 MiB) = 8 MiB, retained <= 128 certificates. Not unbounded.

Tested, and with the exact shape the bead worries about: review_aia_total_fetch_cap (pkix-chain/tests/review_aia.rs:189) sets max_uris_per_cert = 64 against a 64-way fan-out fixture (leaf-fan64.der), sets max_total_fetches = 3, and asserts the fetcher was called exactly 3 times. 64 URIs advertised, 3 fetched. All 17 review_aia tests pass.

Honest residual, not enough to keep this open at P1: pkix-chain counts FETCHES, not BYTES, so a custom AiaFetcher with no per-response cap of its own gives 8 x arbitrary size. pkix-chain cannot cap bytes it has not yet received -- the per-response cap is necessarily the fetchers job, and the shipped fetcher does it at 1 MiB. A caller supplying their own fetcher owns that bound, which is worth a rustdoc sentence on the AiaFetcher trait rather than a byte counter in the loop.
